newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian group wants protection for civilians.
newsitem.headline: Algerian group wants protection for civilians.

text.p: Algeria's official human rights group on Friday called on authorities to ensure the security of civilians after polical violence killed hundreds in the past few weeks.

Algeria's state-owned radio quoted a statement issued by the state Observatoire National des Droits de l'Homme (ONDH) as saying: "The authorities should take all available measures to ensure the security of Algeria's citizens and protect their property within strict respect of the state of law."
The group said the massacres perpetrated against civilians by the "armed Islamic groups" should be denounced.

According to independent sources more than 300 people have died in the past four weeks coinciding with the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan in massacres and bomb attacks in Algiers and neighbouring hamlets and towns.
The authorities blamed Moslem rebels for the deaths.

About 60,000 people have died in Algeria's violence pitting Moslem guerrillas against government forces since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
